planting.note: Smoke-treat or use a smoke primer plus scarification to break seed dormancy before sowing into a sharply drained, low-phosphorus mix.

directions: Grow in lean, acidic, fast-draining soil and avoid phosphorus-rich fertilizers, which this fynbos native cannot tolerate. Give it a sheltered spot with excellent air movement since it is prone to root rot in humid or waterlogged conditions. The nodding cream-to-pink papery bracts, prized in the wedding-flower trade, appear on wiry stems in late winter through spring. Prune lightly after flowering to maintain a dense, bushy habit and extend the plant's productive lifespan.
sources: Pacific Bulb Society / Protea Atlas Project

planting.note: Scarify and smoke-treat seed, then sow in a gritty, nutrient-poor medium kept just moist until germination.

directions: This smaller, finer-textured relative of the Blushing Bride carries clusters of soft pink, papery flowerheads above needle-like, silky-haired foliage. It demands the same lean, phosphorus-free, well-drained soil as other Cape fynbos shrubs and resents heavy clay or summer humidity. Site it where cool air circulates freely and roots stay on the dry side between waterings. Light post-bloom pruning keeps the wiry stems compact and encourages repeat flowering the following season.
